chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

Whoever performs wudu (ablution) and wipes himself will have one good deed written for him; and whoever performs wudu (ablution) and does not wipe himself until his wudu (ablution) dries, Allah will write thirty good deeds for him.

key_terms.تَمَنْدَلَ: wiped himself with a cloth or towel after wudu (ablution)
key_terms.حَسَنَةً: a good deed recorded as reward

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for not drying oneself after wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states the reward for one who performs wudu (ablution) and then wipes himself, and a greater reward for one who leaves the moisture of wudu (ablution) until it dries naturally. It highlights a recommended etiquette connected to ritual purity and the spiritual reward associated with acts of worship.
